niches.title: Archive Answers · Shorts
niches.polish_voice: third-person documentary narration, never address the viewer as 'you' outside the hook
niches.topic_brief: History 'why' explainers for a US audience: the real causes behind 20th-century and older events — the Vietnam War, the Cold War, falling monarchies and collapsing empires, and 'why does X still...' questions with historical roots. Explain CAUSES, not battles. Structure: 0-2s hook = a 'why' question with one concrete detail; context in one breath (who, where, when); 2-3 causes, each a documented fact with a name, date or number; a turn — the cause most people miss; the outro answers the hook. RULES: no graphic violence or casualty descriptions; no current elections, parties or judgments of living politicians; only facts a standard history textbook confirms; causes must be ones mainstream historians name (never present a single contested cause as THE reason); no conspiracy theories.
niches.safety_rule: historical events, wars and politics of the past are fine; no graphic violence or gore, no current elections, political parties or living politicians, no ongoing wars, no medical/financial advice, no conspiracy theories
niches.broll_query_rule: broll_query is a SEARCH QUERY for REAL archival photos (Wikimedia Commons, Library of Congress, National Archives): 3-6 English words naming the concrete subject + place + year or decade, e.g. 'Huey helicopters Vietnam 1966', 'Seward Alaska treaty 1867', 'Saigon street 1968', 'Berlin Wall 1961'. Name real people, places, ships, documents and buildings of that time. For lines about WHERE something is, borders, distances or territory changing hands write a map instead: 'MAP: <country or US state>' or 'MAP: <from> -> <to>' (e.g. 'MAP: Russia -> Alaska', 'MAP: Vietnam'), modern names only. Never ask for combat casualties, bodies, blood, wounded or executions; no abstract scenes, no 3d, no modern stock footage.
